q-52512.name: Question 1
q-52512.worked_solution:
We replace $x$ with $10$ in the given expression, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}h(10) & =\frac{\sqrt{2x+7}}{\sqrt{x-7}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2(10)+7}}{\sqrt{10-7}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{27}}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{27}{3}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

q-63881.name: Question 2
q-63881.worked_solution:
We replace $a$ with $10$ in the given expression, and simplify as much as possible:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{8a+1} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{8\cdot 10+1} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{80+1} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{81} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{27\cdot 3} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{{3}^{3}\cdot 3} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{{3}^{3}}\cdot \sqrt[3]{3} & = \\ 3\sqrt[3]{3} & \end{aligned}
$$

q-82110.name: Question 3
q-82110.worked_solution:
We replace $x$ with $15$ in the given expression, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{x-3} & = \\ \sqrt{15-3} & = \\ \sqrt{12}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify even further using the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{12} & = \\ \sqrt{4\cdot 3} & = \\ \sqrt{{2}^{2}\cdot 3} & = \\ \sqrt{{2}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{3} & = \\ 2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

b
433
c
263
d
4
e
343
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We replace r with 9 in the given expression, and simplify as much as possible: 7r+13=7(9)+13=63+13=643=433=4
